title: Two Lanes Out Of Tulsa
subject: a two-lane road out of town
caption: Country rock in the Nashville tradition. Acoustic guitar and a Telecaster trading fills, pedal steel sustaining under every vocal line, fiddle taking the solo, Hammond organ pad, bass and a relaxed shuffle on the kit. A male baritone sings with a pronounced twang and southern drawl, conversational and unhurried, with a low harmony on the choruses. Warm analog saturation, plate reverb, slapback on the vocal. 98 BPM, G major. Nostalgic, dusty, unhurried.
lyrics:
[Intro - Pedal Steel]

[Verse 1]
Two lanes out of Tulsa and a radio
Playing something my father would've known
The girl at the Conoco called me honey
And I about came apart

[Pre-Chorus]
It don't take much these days

[Chorus]
I ain't running, I'm just driving
There's a difference if you've done both
One of them's got somewhere to be
And one of them just needs the road

[Verse 2]
There's a church sign outside Sapulpa
Says the Lord ain't finished with you yet
Well I hope He's got some patience left
Because I'm slower than most

[Fiddle Solo]

[Chorus]
I ain't running, I'm just driving
There's a difference if you've done both
One of them's got somewhere to be
And one of them just needs the road

[Outro]
Just needs the road
Just needs the road
